newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour says will not cede control to Europe.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour says will not cede control to Europe.

text.p: British opposition Labour's leader Tony Blair said on Tuesday he would not cede control of defense, taxation and immigration to the European Union.
"Defense, taxation, immigration will remain subject to national veto," Blair said at a news conference.
Blair was referring to the European Council meeting in Amsterdam in June at which decisions are expected to be taken on issues which have been discussed at the Intergovernmental Conference (IGC).
The IGC is an ongoing meeting of European Union governmental officials intended to address political issues related to further European integration and eastward expansion of the Union.
Blair said he hoped to reach agreement at the Amsterdam conference, but the only test for Labour policy on Europe would be what was in the British national interest.

"There are plenty of areas in which it is important that Britain's national interest is always going to come first. The people understand that abroad and if they don't understand it, well they will understand it when we get to the negotiations."
Blair added that the vast majority of people in Britain knew the issue was who was going to fight for Britain best.
"You cannot have Britain represented by a political party that is falling apart even in the course of an general election campaign."
